rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Those who take the victory as Islam attach the purpose lam to that victory: Islam and guidance are the cause of forgiveness.
rows.anchor: فتح الله عليك الإسلام ليغفر لك الله، وأبي إسحاق.

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: If the victory is Hudaybiyya, the lam can be an oath lam, meaning God will surely forgive; its form resembles the purpose lam.
rows.anchor: وهو أنه قال هذه اللام لام اليمين، كأنه قال ليغفرن الله لك

rows.speaker: أبو حاتم
rows.claim: He supports the oath-lam reading by analogy with Arabic exclamatory forms that take the jussive because they resemble commands.
rows.anchor: واحتج بأن العرب تقول في التعجب: أطرف بزيد, فيجزمونه لشبهه بلفظ الأمر

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: He rejects Abu Hatim: an oath lam is never kasra and does not cause the subjunctive, so this cannot mean a deleted oath form.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الأنباري: هذا الذي قاله أبو حاتم غلط, لأن لام القسم لا تكسر ولا ينصب بها

rows.speaker: ابن الأنباري
rows.claim: The exclamatory analogy fails because exclamation is deliberately cast in command form, while an oath lam is never found kasra.
rows.anchor: وليس هذا بمنزلة: أطرف بزيد؛ لأن التعجب عدل به إلى لفظ الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو العباس
rows.claim: The lam is purposive: the victory brings forgiveness together with the newly completed blessing, making the purpose construction apt.
rows.anchor: فلما انضم إلى المغفرة شيء حادث واقع حسن معنى كي

rows.speaker: ابن جرير وصاحب النظم
rows.claim: They take the phrase as excerpted from 110:3: after victory, the Prophet was told to glorify and seek forgiveness, and was forgiven.
rows.anchor: هذا مقتص من قوله: {فسبح بحمد ربك واستغفره} [النصر: 3]

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The past sin means what occurred in the pre-Islamic period, and the later sin what occurred after prophethood.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني ما كان في الجاهلية وما تأخر بعد النبوة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains it as pre-Islamic sin and whatever might occur later; this follows those who allow minor sins for prophets.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس: أي ط كان عليك من إثم الجاهلية وما تأخر مما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Ibn Abbas explanation follows the theological position that prophets may commit minor sins.
rows.anchor: وهذا على طريقة من جوز الصغائر على الأنبياء

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: The earlier sin is Adam and Eve’s sin forgiven through the Prophet’s blessing; the later sins are those of his community through his supplication.
rows.anchor: ذنب أبويك آدم وحواء ببركتك، (وما تأخر) يعني: من ذنوب أمتك بدعوتك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He says Ata’s distant reading can be framed by supplying an omitted genitive, making the earlier sin that of the Prophet’s parents.
rows.anchor: يمكن توجيهه على بعد، وهو أن يحمل قوله (من ذنبك) على حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since the Prophet has no sin after prophethood, the attribution must be understood in a way that can validly apply, as Ata’s explanation allows.
rows.anchor: ويبين هذا القول أنه لا ذنب له بعد النبوة

rows.speaker: سفيان الثوري
rows.claim: The earlier sin is what the Prophet did before Islam, while the later refers to what he has not yet done.
rows.anchor: ما عملت في الجاهلية وما تأخر، يعني: ما لم تعمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He questions how something not yet done could be described as forgiven, then explains the wording as emphatic possibility: it would be forgiven if it occurred.
rows.anchor: والجواب: أن هذا يذكر على طريق التأكيد والإمكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The examples of giving to unseen people and striking people not yet met express emphasis and possibility, not literal completed acts.
rows.anchor: كذلك في الآية غفر المتقدم والمتأخر لو وجد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains the completion of God’s blessing as occurring in Paradise.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: في الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Another report from Ibn Abbas takes the completed blessing as prophethood and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: عنه أي: بالنبوة والمغفرة، والمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Victory is joined with complete blessing through forgiveness and guidance to the straight path, Islam.
rows.anchor: ليجتمع لك مع الفتح تمام النعمة بالمغفرة والهداية إلى صراط مستقيم وهو الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentators explain the coming judgment as the coming recompense.
rows.anchor: قالوا: وإن الجزاء لكائن

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: Abu Ishaq specifies that recompense for people’s deeds will certainly occur.
rows.anchor: إن المجازاة على أعمالكم لواقعة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: After recounting the preceding signs, God challenges the polytheists to say whether their idols possess any of the power and grandeur just described of the Lord.
rows.anchor: أخبرونا عن هذه الآلهة التي تعبدونها من دون الله، هل لها من هذه القدرة والعظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, “Have you considered?” functions as a request for information or an answer, as in 6:40.
rows.anchor: على ما ذكر السؤال والاستفتاء كقوله: {قل أرأيتم إن أتاكم عذابه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse coheres with the preceding passage under the interpretation just given.
rows.anchor: وتنتظم الآية بما قبلها على المعنى الذي ذكره

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: He reads the question as asking whether the idols revealed anything to the polytheists as revelation came to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: أفرأيتم هذه الآلهة التي تعبدونهن أأوحين شيئا إليكم كما أوحي إلى النبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first two interpretations are inferred from context, but Abu Ishaq’s contrast between female gods and the males chosen by their worshippers is the strongest of the three.
rows.anchor: وهذا الوجه أجود الثلاثة

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He asks whether these female deities belong to God while the polytheists choose males for themselves, as the following verse says.
rows.anchor: أفرأيتم هذه الإناث ألله هي وأنتم تختارون الذكران وذلك قوله: ألكم الذكر وله الأنثى

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: He parses “Have you considered?” as “tell me”: the verb takes an object and the question occupies the second object position.
rows.anchor: أرأيتم هنا بمنزلة أخبروني لتعدي أرأيت إلى المفعول ووقوع الاستفهام في موضع المفعول الثاني

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: He supplies an omitted idea: have you considered making al-Lat and al-Uzza daughters of God, when you yourselves have sons?
rows.anchor: والمعنى: أرأيتم جعلكم اللات والعزى بنات الله، ألكم الذكر

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: The omitted idea is recoverable because the Qur’an repeatedly states that they assigned daughters to God and called angels female.
rows.anchor: وجاز الحذف لأن هذا قد تكرر في القرآن كقوله: {ويجعلون لله البنات} [النحل: 57]

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: He treats an omitted element in the cited Arabic line as if expressed, since its meaning is understood.
rows.anchor: سيبويه جعل كلا في قوله: ونار توقد بالليل نارا

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Lat is an idol.
rows.anchor: فأما اللات فروى عطاء عن ابن عباس قال: هي صنم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Al-Lat was located in al-Taif.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هي بالطائف

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Lat was a rock at al-Taif worshipped by Thaqif.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: هي صخرة كانت بالطائف # لثقيف (¬1) يعبدونها

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Al-Lat was a house at Nakhlah that Quraysh worshipped.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: اللات بيت بنخلة (¬3) كانت قريش تعبده (¬4)

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Lat was a Quraysh idol inside the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: هي صنم في جوف الكعبة لقريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols’ names have no underlying meanings: they are inert things that can neither harm nor benefit.
rows.anchor: لا ضر عندها ولا نفع فهي تسميات ألقيت على جمادات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “They are only names” refers to al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat, names coined by the polytheists without proof.
rows.anchor: قوله: {إن هي} يعني اللات والعزى ومناة. يقول: ما هي إلا أسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The names were falsely assigned by the polytheists and their forefathers without any warrant from God.
rows.anchor: تسمية باطلة لم يقم بها حجة، وهو قوله: {ما أنزل الله بها من سلطان}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse means God sent no warrant for worshipping these idols.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون المعنى: ما أنزل الله بعبادتها من سلطان

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: No scripture was sent giving them proof for their claim that the idols are gods.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: لم ينزل بذلك كتابا لكم فيه حجة بما تقولون إنها آلهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They follow conjecture in worship, having no knowledge that the idols are gods, along with their own desires.
rows.anchor: ما لهم من علم أنها آلهة إلا ظنا يتبعون في عبادتها الظن وهوى النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their desires are what Satan has made attractive to them.
rows.anchor: وهو ما زين لهم الشيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance from their Lord means the clarification and right guidance brought by the Book and the Messenger.
rows.anchor: أي البيان والرشاد بالكتاب والرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage expresses amazement that they continued worshipping the idols despite the clarity of the proof.
rows.anchor: وهذا تعجيب من حالهم حيث لم يتركوا عبادتها مع وضوح البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next passage also rebukes the disbelievers for wishing that idols would intercede for them.
rows.anchor: ثم أنكر على الكفار تمنيتهم شفاعة الأصنام

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: When 17:110 was revealed, Meccan disbelievers said they knew only Musaylima, the Rahman of al-Yamama; 25:60 records their denial of the name.
rows.anchor: قال كفار مكة: ما نعرف إلا مسيلمة، رحمان اليمامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God identifies himself by mentioning his works so that people will recognize him and affirm his oneness.
rows.anchor: فأخبر الله عن نفسه، وذكر صنعه ليعرف فيوحد

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: Although “taught” normally takes two objects, only one is stated; the recipient is understood, as in saying that Zayd fed food.
rows.anchor: قوله (علم) يقتضي مفعولين ولم يجيء هاهنا إلا واحد

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: God taught the Qur’an to Muhammad, who in turn taught it to his community.
rows.anchor: علم القرآن محمدا وعلمه محمد -صلى الله عليه وسلم- أمته

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He explains teaching the Qur’an as making it easy to remember or recite.
rows.anchor: ومعنى {علم القرآن} يسره لأن يذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Created the human” is coordinated as another assertion confirming the preceding statement, without a conjunction.
rows.anchor: ثم نسق على هذا خبرا آخر مؤكدا له من غير حرف عطف

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The human created is Muhammad, and the taught expression is eloquent speech, meaning the Qur’an.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد محمدا -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

rows.speaker: ابن كيسان
rows.claim: He also identifies the human as Muhammad, but says the taught expression is knowledge of past and future events, including Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: إلا أنه قال في البيان أنه بيان ما كان وما يكون

rows.speaker: الكلبي وقتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: They identify the human as Adam, to whom God taught the names of everything.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي وقتادة: الإنسان آدم -عليه السلام- علمه أسماء كل شيء، وهذا قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: أبو العالية ومرة وابن زيد والحسن والقرظي والسدي ويمان بن رباب
rows.claim: They take “the human” as humankind collectively and “expression” as speech, discernment, writing, understanding, communication, and the language given to each people, distinguishing humans from animals.
rows.anchor: وقال آخرون: الإنسان اسم لجنس الناس جميعا، ومعنى {علمه البيان} النطق والتمييز، والكتابة والخط

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: He reads “dhu al-jalal” in the nominative, making it agree with “name”; this indicates that the name is the named one, since majesty is God’s attribute, not an attribute of naming.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر: ذو الجلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Glorifying God here means declaring him free of what people say in describing him.
rows.anchor: أي فبرئ الله عز وجل مما يقولون في وصفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks why they fail to act when the soul or spirit reaches the throat at death.
rows.anchor: يقول فهلا إذا بلغت الروح أو النفس الحلقوم عند الموت

rows.speaker: أهل المعاني
rows.claim: God is closer by knowledge, power, and sight: he sees the dying person without distance, whereas other observers are separated by distance; the disbelievers do not know this.
rows.anchor: أي بالعلم والقدرة والرؤية وذلك أن الله تعالى يراه من غير مسافة بينه وبينه

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: “We are closer” refers instead to the Angel of Death and his assistants, who take the soul and are unseen by those addressed.
rows.anchor: وقال المفسرون: {ونحن أقرب} يعني ملك الموت وأعوانه

rows.speaker: عطاء وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد ومقاتل
rows.claim: Most commentators take “not subject to recompense” to mean not held accountable.
rows.anchor: قال أكثر المفسرين: غير محاسبين وهو قول عطاء، وسعيد بن جبير، ومجاهد، ومقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as meaning not owned.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي: غير مملوكين

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as meaning not recompensed.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: غير مجزيين

rows.speaker: الفراء والزجاج
rows.claim: They prefer the phrase to mean “not owned”; the accompanying lexical note says “madina” means an enslaved woman.
rows.anchor: واختار الفراء والزجاج غير مملوكين (¬4)، والمدينة: الأمة المملوكة.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Akhtal’s phrase “ibn madina” is cited as poetic evidence for the sense of an enslaved person.
rows.anchor:
وأنشد أبو عبيدة للأخطل (¬5):
ربت فربا في كرمها ابن مدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Return it” means return the soul that has reached the throat.
rows.anchor: أي تردون تلك النفس التي بلغت الحلقوم

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: One answer, “return it,” answers both conditional challenges; he compares the construction with 2:38, where one response answers two conditions.
rows.anchor: وأجيب {فلولا إذا بلغت} و {فلولا إن كنتم} بجواب واحد، وهو قوله: {ترجعونها}

rows.speaker: صاحب النظم
rows.claim: If, as they claim, they are not accountable or recompensed and there is no resurrection, why can they not return a loved one’s soul? Their inability shows that control belongs to God.
rows.anchor: فلم لا يدلكم ذلك على أن الأمر إلى غيركم وهو الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: If they are not owned or governed and can delay a death as they claim, they should return the soul or avert death; their inability disproves their claim.
rows.anchor: فهلا ترجعون الروح إذا بلغت الحلقوم وهلا تردون عن أنفسكم الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having established that people are accountable, recompensed, and owned, the discussion turns to the kinds of people at death and their death rattles.
rows.anchor: ذكر طبقات الخلق عند الموت والحشرجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening phrase follows the explanation already given earlier.
rows.anchor: {هو الله} وهو ظاهر التفسير ماض فيما سبق

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: They explain “the Holy” as pure from every defect and transcendent above what is unsuitable for God.
rows.anchor: هو الطاهر من كل عيب، المنزه مما لا يليق به

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains “the Holy” as the source of blessings.
rows.anchor: في قوله: {القدوس} الذي منه البركات

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He also understands “the Holy” as blessed, citing the expression “sanctified land” to mean blessed land.
rows.anchor: ويقال أرض مقدسة، أي مباركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The Peace” is explained in two ways: God is free from deficiency and defect, or he keeps his creation safe from injustice.
rows.anchor: ذكروا فيه قولين: أحدهما: أنه الذي سلم من النقص والعيب

rows.speaker: أبو قتادة
rows.claim: Asked by Abu Qatada, the Prophet explained the best in deeds as the one most complete in intellect, most fearful of God, and most discerning about divine commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قال أبو قتادة (¬2): سألت رسول الله -صلى الله عليه وسلم- عنه فقال: "يقول: أيكم أحسن عقلا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada similarly defines the best as most complete in intellect, most abstinent from God’s prohibitions, and quickest to obey.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال قتادة: أتم عقلا، وأورع عن محارم الله، وأسرع في طاعة الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good works may be explained through complete intellect because sound action follows from intellect, as the Prophet’s report indicates.
rows.anchor: وإنما جاز أن يفسر حسن العمل بتمام العقل؛ لأنه يترتب على العقل

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He explains the best in deeds as the person most ascetic toward and least attached to worldly life.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الحسن: أيكم أزهد في الدنيا وأترك لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in punishing those who disobey without reflecting on creation or deriving his oneness and power from it; he forgives those who repent and do so.
rows.anchor: {الغفور} لمن تاب إليه، واستدل بصنيعه على توحيده

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والمفسرون
rows.claim: The seven heavens are arranged one above another.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس والمفسرون: بعضها فوق بعض

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Each heaven is dome-shaped and its edges touch the next; the lowest heaven lies over the earth like a dome.
rows.anchor: كل سماء مقببة على الأخرى يلتصق بها أطرافها

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He parses “in layers” as a verbal noun: the heavens were layered in layers.
rows.anchor: و {طباقا} مصدر، أي: طوبقت طباقا

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The verse means that no defect can be seen in the creation of the heavens.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: ما ترى يا ابن آدم في خلق السموات من عيب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as absence of flaws and variation.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: ما ترى خللا واختلافا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: He explains it as absence of difference or defect, so an observer cannot say that something would have been better otherwise.
rows.anchor:
وقال السدي: {من تفاوت} أي من اختلاف وعيب (¬7)، يقول الناظر:
لو كان كذا كان أحسن

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He explains the phrase as creation not having parts that fall short of or miss one another.
rows.anchor: قال الكلبي: هو الذي يفوت بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text is also read “tafut”; both readings have the same meaning, like the paired forms “tasʿar/tasaʿar” and “taʿahhadta/taʿahhadta.”
rows.anchor: وتقرأ (تفوت) (¬3) قال الفراء: وهما بمنزلة واحدة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He glosses the word as difference or variation.
rows.anchor: والتفاوت: الاختلاف، يريد: هل ترى في خلقه من اختلاف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He gives the same explanation of the verse.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال الزجاج سواء

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He explains it as disorder and variation, deriving the word from one thing missing another and thereby causing a flaw, though creation remains interconnected.
rows.anchor: أصله من الفوت، وهو أن يفوت شيء شيئا، فيقع الخلل فيهن

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: He prefers “tafāwut” because Arabic speakers commonly say that something varies, but rarely use the alternate form for that meaning.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن الأخفش: تفاوت أجود، لأنهم يقولون: تفاوت

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: He prefers “tafut,” meaning that a thing has been missed or omitted, and cites a report about a man taking his father’s property.
rows.anchor: واختار أبو عبيد (¬2): (تفوت)، قال: يقال: تفوت الشيء إذا فات.

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: “Return your gaze” means look again; al-Farra gives the same explanation, since the preceding phrase asks what one sees.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل (¬4): اردد البصر

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: “Any breaks” means fissures, cracks, splits, gaps, or holes.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: من فروج وصدوع وشقوق وفتوق وخروق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: “Twice” means again and again, one time after another.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد مرة بعد مرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He explains the gaze returning humbled as returning in a small or abased state; al-Farra and al-Zajjaj agree.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: صاغرا

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He explains “humbled” as driven away, from the expression for shooing a dog away.
rows.anchor: مبعدا من قولك: خسأت الكلب إذا باعدته

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: The gaze is driven away and diminished, like someone who intends an attack but is frightened off and fails.
rows.anchor: الخاسئ: المبعد المصغر -والله أعلم- كالذي قصد ففزع

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas clarifies that the humbled gaze is one that fails to see what it had hoped to see.
rows.anchor: الخاسئ: الذي لم ير ما يهوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Tame” describes something compliant and subdued; its verbal noun is submission and gentleness, as with a tame riding animal.
rows.anchor: الذلول من كل شيء: المنقاد الذي يذل لك. ومصدره الذل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The earth is made easy for people, without roughness or steepness that prevents walking.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: سهل لكم الأرض

rows.speaker: مقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: The earth is made tame by being fixed with mountains so that it does not move with its inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: أثبتها بالجبال لئلا تزول بأهلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Walk through its slopes” is a permissive command and explains how the earth is made compliant.
rows.anchor: قوله: {فامشوا في مناكبها} أمر إباحة

rows.speaker: قتادة والضحاك وابن عباس
rows.claim: They explain the earth’s “slopes” as its mountains and hillocks, named for their resemblance to the raised shoulders of a person.
rows.anchor: أنها الجبال، وهو قول قتادة والضحاك وابن عباس. قالوا: جبالها وآكامها

rows.speaker: مجاهد والكلبي ومقاتل والحسن وعطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They explain the “slopes” as regions, roads, passes, edges, and sides; al-Farra and Ibn Qutayba choose this view.
rows.anchor: أنها النواحي والطرق والفجاج والأطراف والجوانب

rows.speaker: الفراء وابن قتيبة
rows.claim: They prefer “slopes” to mean the earth’s sides, just as a person’s two shoulders are his sides.
rows.anchor: قال: {مناكبها}: جوانبها، ومنكبا الرجل جانباه

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: He reports both explanations but prefers mountains: if walking on earth is easy, walking through its mountains demonstrates its tameness even more.
rows.anchor: واختار القول الأول وقال: أشبه التفسير من قال في جبالها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Eat from its provision” means consume what God has created for people as provision on earth.
rows.anchor: أي مما خلقه رزقا لكم في الأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The provision includes what God grows for people in plains and mountains.
rows.anchor: يريد ما أنبت لكم في السهل والجبل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: “To him is the resurrection” means people will be raised from their graves to God.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: وإلى الله تبعثون من قبوركم

rows.speaker: أبو إسحاق
rows.claim: The creator of the flawless heavens and tamed earth is able to raise people from the dead.
rows.anchor: الذي خلق السموات بلا تفاوت وذلل الأرض قادر أن ينشركم ويبعثكم

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The warning asks whether people feel secure from the punishment and torment of the one in heaven.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: يعني عقوبة من في السماء وعذاب من في السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “The one in heaven” means God’s dominion, sovereignty, and power; the wording magnifies his authority, not a location or direction for God.
rows.anchor: من في السماء سلطانه وملكه وقدرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparable statement that God is in the heavens and earth means that events there occur by his permission and will, and nothing is hidden from him.
rows.anchor: ما يجري فيهما بإذنه وإرادته لا يخفى عليه شيء منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God cannot be in a place or described as having a direction.
rows.anchor: لاستحالة أن يكون الله تعالى في مكان أو موصوفا بجهة

rows.speaker: بعض أهل المعاني
rows.claim: Some instead identify the one in heaven as the angel assigned to punishment, Gabriel, who causes the earth to swallow people by God’s command.
rows.anchor: {من في السماء} هو الملك (¬6) الموكل بالعذاب وهو جبريل

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: He explains “how was my rejection?” as God’s alteration and denial, and says the people found the punishment to be true.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: تغييري وإنكاري أليس وجدوا العذاب حقا

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: The birds spread their wings in the air, then draw them back toward themselves.
rows.anchor: قال المفسرون: تصف أجنحتها في الهواء. {ويقبضن}، أي: يقبضنها إلى أنفسها بعد الصف

rows.speaker: ابن قتيبة
rows.claim: He explains the birds’ movement as striking their sides with their wings.
rows.anchor: قال ابن قتيبة: يضربن بها جنوبهن

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: This describes flight: spreading the wing, then contracting it after it has been spread.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى الطيران، وهو بسط الجناح وقبضها بعد البسط

rows.speaker: أبو خراش
rows.claim: His cited poem describes a bird driving its wing through extension and contraction, illustrating the birds’ motion.
rows.anchor: يحث الجناح بالتبسط والقبض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “And they contract” is coordinated with “spreading” in the sense “and contracting”; the two motions show how birds remain aloft despite their weight and size.
rows.anchor: وعطف قوله: {ويقبضن} على {صافات} لأن معناه: وقابضات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is who holds and subdues the air so that the birds remain suspended in both spreading and contracting; only the All-Merciful holds them.
rows.anchor: من الذي أمسكها وسخر لها الهواء؟ وهو معنى قوله: {ما يمسكهن إلا الرحمن}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same sign appears in 16:79, where birds are described as being held in the sky.
rows.anchor: وهذا كقوله: {ألم يروا إلى الطير مسخرات في جو السماء} الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Despite clear proofs, disbelievers persist in rejecting faith as if they could fend off God’s punishment with an army; the question denies that they have such protection.
rows.anchor: صاروا كأنهم يمتنعون من عذاب الله بجند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The army question continues the preceding question about security from the one in heaven; “army” is singular in form, hence “this that is an army.”
rows.anchor: وهذا نسق على قوله: {أم أمنتم من في السماء}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: No army can protect the people from God if he intends to punish them.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس ينصركم مني إن أردت عذابكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are deluded by Satan, who persuades them that punishment will not descend on them.
rows.anchor: من الشيطان يغرهم بأن العذاب لا ينزل بهم

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The question about provision asks which of their gods can provide rain if God withholds it.
rows.anchor: أي: من الذي يرزقكم من آلهتكم المطر إن أمسكه الله عنكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They persist in tyranny and turn away from faith instead of reflecting or taking heed.
rows.anchor: ليسوا يعتبرون ولا يتفكرون، لجوا في طغيانهم وتماديهم وتباعدهم عن الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person who walks face-down represents disbelievers, wandering in error and blind of heart; the upright person sees the road and walks Islam’s straight path.
rows.anchor: فضرب المكب على وجهه مثلا للكفار؛ لأنه أكب على وجهه في الغي والكفر يمشي ضالا أعمى القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Bending face-down” is the causative/reflexive form of casting someone down; it is also said of one wandering heedlessly in error.
rows.anchor: والإكباب مطاوع الكب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي ومقاتل ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: They identify the straight path as Islam and describe the believer as walking upright and seeing the way.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عباس في رواية الكلبي، وقول مقاتل، ومجاهد، والضحاك

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: He depicts the disbeliever as following his own head into disbelief and misguidance like a beast.
rows.anchor: راكبا رأسه في الكفر والضلالة كما تركب البهيمة رأسها

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The two figures are Abu Jahl and the Prophet.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني أبا جهل والنبي -صلى الله عليه وسلم-

rows.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: The two figures are Abu Jahl and Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء عن ابن عباس: يريد أبا جهل وحمزة بن عبد المطلب

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: The two figures are Abu Jahl and Ammar ibn Yasir.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة (¬1): هو أبو جهل وعمار بن ياسر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: He applies the image to the hereafter: the disbeliever is resurrected face-down, while the believer walks upright, as in 17:97.
rows.anchor: هذا في الآخرة يحشر الله الكافر مكبا على وجهه يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A mark is the trace of cauterization; a person may also be marked by a cut in the ear as an identifying sign.
rows.anchor: الوسم: أثر كية. يقال: وسمته فهو موسوم بسمة يعرف بها

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد
rows.claim: He says “trunk” means the nose and cites Dhu al-Rumma’s poem as evidence for the plural form referring to noses.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيد: الخرطوم الأنف. وأنشد قول ذي الرمة

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: He also defines khartum and khatm as the nose.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو زيد: الخرطوم والخطم: الأنف

rows.speaker: المبرد
rows.claim: He says the word here means the nose; related terms for the snout or mouth differ among people, predators, hooved animals, and camels.
rows.anchor: وقال المبرد: الخرطوم هاهنا الأنف

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators take the mark as a threat that will be carried out in the hereafter.
rows.anchor: واختلفوا في معنى هذا الوسم، فالأكثرون على أنه وعيد (¬8) له بذلك في الآخرة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: The mark will blacken the nose; the person’s face will be black before he enters the Fire.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: سنسمه بالسواد على الأنف، وذلك أنه يسود وجهه قبل دخول النار

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: He similarly says the face will be blackened as an identifying mark in the afterlife; al-Farra and al-Zajjaj choose this explanation.
rows.anchor: ونحو هذا قال أبو العالية: يسود وجهه فيجعل له علما في # الآخرة ويعرف بسواد وجهه

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: He explains it as the mark of the people of the Fire, blackening the face; naming the nose stands for the whole face.
rows.anchor: سنسمه سمة أهل النار؛ أي: سنسود وجهه

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: He says the mark identifies the people of the Fire by their blackened faces; a distinct mark may also single out this man for his exceptional hostility to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: وجائز -والله أعلم- أن ينفرد بسمة؛ لتعاليه في عداوة النبي

rows.speaker: الضحاك وابن عباس في رواية عطاء والكسائي
rows.claim: They understand the mark as a brand on the face by which he will be recognized in the afterlife, like sheep are branded; al-Kisa'i chooses this view.
rows.anchor: وجعل الضحاك هذه السمة كيا على وجهه يعرف بها في الآخرة
